questions.question: What do the letters ETL stand for in data engineering?
options: Encode, Transfer, Load
Extract, Transform, Load
Execute, Test, Launch
Export, Transform, Log
questions.explanation: ETL is the core data pipeline pattern: Extract data from sources (APIs, databases, files), Transform it (clean, join, aggregate, reshape), and Load it into a destination (data warehouse, database, file). Most data engineering work is building and maintaining ETL pipelines.

questions.question: In a data pipeline, why should the Transform step be separated from the Extract step?
options: Because transformation requires a different programming language
To allow re-running transformations on raw data without re-fetching from the source
Because databases cannot store untransformed data
Because Python can only do one operation at a time
questions.explanation: Storing raw extracted data before transforming it (the 'raw layer') lets you fix transformation bugs and reprocess data without re-calling the API or re-downloading files. This separation also makes debugging easier—if output is wrong, you can inspect raw data to determine whether the error was in extraction or transformation.

questions.question: Which pandas operation is most useful in the Transform step when combining data from multiple source files?
options: df.describe()
pd.concat() or pd.merge()
df.plot()
df.to_csv()
questions.explanation: `pd.concat()` stacks DataFrames with the same columns (vertical union), while `pd.merge()` joins DataFrames on shared keys (like SQL JOIN). Both are essential in ETL's Transform step when combining data from multiple sources—e.g., merging sales data with customer data on customer_id.

questions.question: A pipeline fails during the Load step after successfully transforming 10,000 rows. What design pattern minimizes the need to reprocess all rows?
options: Rerun the entire pipeline from Extract every time
Use idempotent loads with checkpointing—track which records were loaded successfully
Skip the failed rows and proceed with the next batch
Store all data in memory until the entire pipeline succeeds
questions.explanation: Idempotent pipelines produce the same result whether run once or multiple times—using upserts (INSERT OR REPLACE) or tracking watermarks. Checkpointing records progress so a failed run can resume from the last successful point rather than restarting from scratch. This is essential for production data pipelines.

questions.question: What is the best way to schedule a Python ETL pipeline to run automatically every day at 6 AM?
options: Use `time.sleep(86400)` in an infinite loop
Use a scheduler like cron (Linux) or a workflow tool like Airflow or Prefect
Set a reminder to manually run the script each morning
Use `threading.Timer` to delay execution by 24 hours
questions.explanation: Cron (system scheduler) or workflow orchestrators like Apache Airflow/Prefect handle scheduling, retries, alerting, and dependency management for production pipelines. `time.sleep()` loops are fragile—they fail silently, don't handle retries, and stop if the process restarts.
